classification.difficultyReason: Requires inverting two different branches and deriving their separate inverse domains from disjoint original ranges.

content.prompt:
Let $f(x)$ be a piecewise-defined function given by
$$f(x)=\begin{cases}\dfrac{x+2}{2}&\text{if }x>1,\\[4pt]\dfrac{2}{2x-3}&\text{if }x\leq1.\end{cases}$$
Find $f^{-1}(x)$.

inlines.text: Invert each branch separately; its original range becomes its inverse domain.

answer.worked:
The linear branch has range $(\frac32,\infty)$. The reciprocal branch has range $[-2,0)$: it equals $-2$ at $x=1$ and approaches $0$ from below as $x\to-\infty$. Each branch is one-to-one and their ranges are disjoint, so $f^{-1}$ exists.

For the linear branch, interchange variables:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac{y+2}{2}\\2x&=y+2\\y&=2x-2\end{align*}$$
This inverse branch applies when $x>\frac32$.

For the reciprocal branch:
$$\begin{align*}x&=\frac2{2y-3}\\2xy-3x&=2\\2xy&=3x+2\\y&=\frac{3x+2}{2x}\end{align*}$$
This inverse branch applies when $-2\leq x<0$.

Therefore
$$f^{-1}(x)=\begin{cases}2x-2&\text{if }x>\dfrac32,\\[4pt]\dfrac{3x+2}{2x}&\text{if }-2\leq x<0.\end{cases}$$
